verification_report.summary:
Sequentially audited every statement and proof in the chapter, with 15 statement-check records and 6 reference-check records. No critical mathematical error or proof gap was found under the explicitly accepted local inputs. The book conventions confirm n>=1, canonical quasi-plurisubharmonic representatives, arbitrary smooth real theta, and the stated dd^c normalization.

Product permanence and vertical convexity are valid. The frozen-form Kiselman argument uses a quadratic potential for beta+eta*kappa, never for theta itself. Locality of current positivity justifies the limit as eta tends to zero despite shrinking coordinate balls. Connectedness gives the global dichotomy; Fubini and supporting affine lower bounds exclude collapse on bounded time intervals. Dominated convergence proves interior L1 continuity, and canonical comparison upgrades the endpoint chord inequality from almost everywhere to everywhere. Joint boundary control remains valid at poles.

The Perron construction correctly regularizes on the product. The jointly upper semicontinuous chord bounds the regularized supremum, while a genuine competitor prevents degenerate slices. Endpoint attainment uses an actual L1-attaining competitor. Joint boundary inequalities justify gluing the maximum at subinterval seams, so maximality proves restriction compatibility. For equal ordinary types, the explicit maximum barrier supplies endpoint attainment and two-sided estimates; convex secant slopes give the stated C-Lipschitz time bound away from common poles.

The smooth block matrix, its 1/2 and 1/4 factors, the Schur complement, and the coefficient n in the wedge equation are correct. Independently, varying the raw action and applying Stokes to the entire form f^2*T retains both mixed first-derivative torsion terms and the (n/2)*f^2*dd^c T term with the stated signs. Necessity and sufficiency follow from unrestricted small endpoint-fixed variations. For n=1, T=1 and all torsion terms vanish. Nonzero translations are Perron segments and solve smooth HCMA; they are stationary exactly when dd^c(omega_u^(n-1))=0.

The cited local results match the supplied SGPT sources; the online [SGPT manuscript](https://mingchenxia.github.io/Lectures/SGPT.pdf) also corroborates the minimum and restriction inputs. Arxiv theorem search was performed first, with web fallback for unmatched queries. No closed-background global Perron, full-mass, energy, or metric-existence theorem was imported. The earlier book chapter_mass.tex supports the nonclosed Stokes step.

Two non-substantive clarifications: the superscript ',2' is an evident extra-comma typo for the squared velocity, fixed unambiguously by the derivation; and Gauduchon preservation under potential perturbations does hold in dimension two, whereas the concluding general nonpreservation observation is valid in higher dimension. Neither affects the proved statements. Detailed deductions and source comparisons are persisted in memory/hermitian_perron_rays_01. The book sources were left unchanged.
